newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee errors prompt stand down order. [CORRECTED 20:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee errors prompt stand down order. [CORRECTED 20:30 GMT]

text.p: A work stoppage has been ordered at the Maine Yankee nuclear plant after operators pumped 10,000 gallons of radioactive water into the wrong tank, officials said Thursday.

Plant managers ordered the stand down at the facility - which is off-line because of safety problems - after consulting with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission about three operator errors in less than a week (corrects to show that the plant ordered the stand down, not the NRC).
"It's a measure you implement to preclude problems from happening that could result in something very significant," said Jimi Yerokum, the NRC's resident inspector at Maine Yankee.

According to an NRC report, plant operators opened the wrong valve and pumped 10,000 gallons of radioactive water from a pit adjacent to the reactor into a storage tank rather than the reciruclation system.
The incident did not result in workers being exposed to additional radiation, according to Yerokum, but he said regulators want to determine how the mistake was allowed to occur.
The stand down was ordered Monday and will remain in effect pending an investigation by an NRC review team.

Maine Yankee is off-line and conducting only minor repair work while its owners decide if the plant can be sold or should be shut down permanently. The plant has been plagued by safety and equipment problems for the past three years.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro, five percent by Maine Public Service Co., four percent by Commonwealth Electric Co, four percent by Eastern Utilities Associates and two percent by Central Vermont Public Service.
